title: deno-kcp Open Architecture
description: Open Architecture document for deno-kcp. Every node is a system context {upstream, overlay, orchestrator}, laid out as trees; refs are plain prefixed id strings.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, relative to the document.

upstreams.description: External artifacts this repo builds on, keyed by up.* id.

orchestrators.description: Things that execute a system context (scripts, binaries, harnesses), keyed by orch.* id.

types.description: Shared Go types of api/v1alpha1 used by more than one kind, keyed by type.* id.

system_contexts.description: Trees of system contexts; the first is the repo, later ones are downstream contexts whose upstream is it.

ref.description: Any ref; a kind context ref may continue with .spec|.status[.field], a type ref with .field. Validator resolves it.

ref-type.description: Shared type id: Go type name, or kebab when no Go type exists.

ref-sc.description: System context id; dot separated kebab segments.

ref-kind-object.description: Whole spec or status of a kind context.

carried.description: Refs, or kcp resources as group/version/resource when no context in this document defines them.

path.description: Repo-relative path, optionally with :Symbol where Symbol is an identifier (dotted allowed) present in the file. Validator checks the file exists and contains Symbol as a whole word.

paths.description: One path or a list of paths.

code.description: Code location: one path, a list, or a map of role to path(s).

order.description: Order the candidates are tried in.

src.description: metadata.src key naming the source document.

basis.description: What a claim rests on when not read directly from code.

axis-entry.description: What carries one axis of the document: a top-level section, a ref prefix, or an id suffix. The validator checks each names something present, so an axis cannot point at nothing.

prefix.description: Ref prefix or prefixes whose ids are the axis members.

suffix.description: Suffix that marks a system context id as a member of the axis.

axes.description: The axes the document is sliced along, keyed by axis name, each naming what carries it, so a reader never has to infer the mapping.

concepts.description: The kind contexts and the shared types.

format.description: metadata.src key of the specification the document follows.

layout.description: How the system context trees are laid out.

roots.description: Entry points nothing references besides the top-level trees; each MUST still be unreferenced.

src.description: Source document index: key to URL or repo-relative path.

go.description: Go version the artifact's go.mod declares, i.e. the toolchain its build requires.

path.description: Path relative to repo (may leave it via ..).

pin.description: How the version in use is fixed; data only, nothing enforces it.

by.description: go_mod: go.mod line; git_submodule: submodule commit; binary_on_path: whatever the name resolves to (unpinned); sibling_path: whatever commit the org-root checkout has (unpinned).

override.description: Env var that replaces the binary.

preflight.description: path_only: the preflight target checks the bare name on PATH and ignores override.

source.description: Where the pin is written in this repo, as path:LINE.

order.description: Resolution order of the binary actually used; the pin is only the last resort when listed last.

executes.description: How it is executed or imported: the call or import site(s).

id.description: Id, when written inline where used.

stop_state.description: State directory the stop script defaults to, when it differs from state.

bin.description: Binary resolution order: a bare name, or the order tried for a built binary.

imports.description: Go package a separate module exists to import across a module boundary.

used_by.description: Callers: the files that invoke it.

env.description: Env var or vars it reads.

composes.description: Orchestrators it invokes: ref, or inline with id when used only here.

requires.description: Upstreams that must be present for it to run.

detached.description: How the started process outlives the script that started it.

ready.description: What the start waits for before reporting it is up.

already_up.description: Condition under which a second start does nothing.

sets_env.description: Env vars it sets for its children.

cluster.description: Cluster it runs against: own when the target starts kine and kcp itself, existing when it drives a cluster someone else started, none when it needs no cluster.

decides.description: Env value to outcome when a live prerequisite is missing.

field-types.description: Field to type.* ref, kind object ref, Go type string, or a single-use type inline with id.

type-entry.description: Shared Go type (struct fields or string enum).

id.description: Id, when written inline where used.

held_by.description: Kind fields holding a value of it.

validate.description: What the gate rejects; anything else passes.

default.description: Value in effect when the field holding this type is absent.

defaults.description: Field to the value in effect when the field is absent; a field not listed defaults to its Go zero value.

zero_default.description: Every field of the type defaults to its Go zero value when absent.

unread.description: Fields no code path reads a value from.

grants.description: Boundaries it authenticates into or signs for; [] when none inside this system.

secret.description: True when disclosure is a compromise.

issued_by.description: Context or orchestrator that mints it.

issued_at.description: The moment it comes into being.

reissue.description: The event that makes a new one in place of this one; none when it is made once.

renewal.description: What renews it in place while it is still valid; none when no code path renews it.

ttl.description: Lifetime: a bare duration, or how it is set.

from.description: Flag or field the lifetime comes from.

default.description: Value used when nobody sets one (a guessable secret).

file_mode.description: Mode of the file it rests in, when it rests in one.

at.description: Where it sits: a location template, or the precedence that picks the file.

file_default.description: Default file when no source names one.

else_create.description: What is created when no source has it.

carried_as.description: Env var, flag, header or file names it travels under.

manifest.description: Upstream written inline: a kind (APIResourceSchema + Go types), a provider component or interface (Go source), a script/workflow field of an example manifest, or a single-use external artifact (path + pin). Keys beyond the listed ones mirror that document.

short.description: Short name kubectl accepts for the resource (APIResourceSchema names.shortNames).

refs.description: Spec field to the kind or kind field it names.

condition_facts.description: Condition type to the code that sets it and the reasons it holds each status, keyed by the types in conditions.

cleared_by.description: Code that removes it; absent when it is only ever re-set, never cleared.

replaced_each_pass.description: The pass replaces the whole condition list, so a condition that no longer applies is dropped.

status_facts.description: Status field to what writes it, when it changes, and the condition or phase a reader decides the same fact from; keyed by exactly the fields in status.

when.description: The transition the field changes on.

decides.description: self when the field is the decision, a condition type it mirrors, or none when nothing is decided from it.

also.description: Field that must be read with this one; this field alone does not carry the fact.

unset_phases.description: Declared phase values no code path writes; the phase starts empty instead.

finalizer.description: Finalizer the kind's teardown waits on.

set_by.description: Who puts it on the object: the example manifests (metadata.finalizers) and/or the provider.

field.description: Manifest field holding the script or workflow; a map of file name to field when it differs per file.

libs.description: Upstream libraries the code is built on.

implements.description: Interface context the code implements: ref, or the interface context inline.

overlay.description: Named data applied to target; inline in the overlay list of the context using it.

target.description: What the data is applied to; absent = the enclosing context's upstream.

manifest.description: Example manifest file(s) this overlay is; data holds the spec fields that matter.

source.description: Code or script file(s) the data is read from.

object.description: The real kcp object an instance context is.

kind.description: Kind; must match the kind reached via upstream.

system-context.description: System context: id, the triple, its trust boundary, plus optional attributes.

upstream.description: Upstream: ref, the upstream context inline, or the manifest inline.

overlay.description: Overlays applied in order, inline where first used, ref elsewhere; [] when none.

orchestrator.description: Executor: orch.* or sc.* ref, or a single-use orchestrator inline with id.

context.description: Innermost execution context (trust boundary) it runs or is stored in.

owns.description: Kinds the provider creates with an ownerReference to this kind.

owned_by.description: Kinds whose reconciler creates this kind with an ownerReference.

maps.description: Mapping the kind performs: from, to, and how the target is chosen.

toolchain.description: Upstream toolchain the context is built with.

runtime.description: Upstream runtime that executes the upstream code (not itself the upstream).

also_run_by.description: Other orchestrators that start this context the same way.

depends_on.description: Contexts that must be up first.

introduces.description: Contexts this one brings into being, inline.

source.description: File or directory the context is read from.

flows.description: Application-level edges between the contexts under this one, keyed by flow.* id.

signs.description: Contexts whose certificate this one signs, top-down: an OpenBao server context lists the OpenBao instances it holds intermediates for, an OpenBao instance the pods that get a leaf from it.

spec_from.description: Kind field whose value the provider copies into this context's spec.

optional.description: Context is not required for the parent to run.

harness.description: Test files under this context: the file, the example or code path it drives, the objects it creates, and the test functions that check the invariant.

funcs.description: Test functions; each names the invariant it checks.

drives.description: Example manifests or code paths it drives.

creates.description: Contexts or kinds whose objects it creates.

role.description: What a file with no test function is for.

serves.description: HTTP surface this context must serve for this repo's examples to work: the path, the refs that call or probe it, and the example manifest that requires it.

path.description: URL path served, as the caller writes it.

required_by.description: Refs that call or probe it.

threat-model.description: Living threat model overlay: execution contexts (one nested tree), credentials, crossings grouped by the context that performs them, and risks ordered by severity.

contexts.description: Root execution context; the rest nest under it in children.

credentials.description: Secrets and tokens, keyed by cred.* id.

crossings.description: Crossings grouped by the system context, orchestrator, or overlay code performing them: what that performer reaches.

additionalProperties.description: Crossings of one performer, keyed by x.* id.

addresses.description: Every address form the system uses, keyed by name: its shape, who writes and reads it, source precedence, and the unresolved case.

surfaces.description: Every artifact the system leaves behind that a human or another program can read, keyed by name: its writer, location, contents, lifetime and readers.

failures.description: Every way the system fails, keyed by name: what triggers it, the signal a human or program sees, what alerts, and the risk recorded for a failure with no signal.

risks.description: Verified weaknesses keyed by r.* id, high to info.

identity.description: The identity systems this repo touches, keyed by name, and the value forms where they meet.

address.description: One address form: its shape, who forms and connects to it, the sources that set it in order, and what happens when it does not resolve.

written_by.description: Contexts or code that form the address.

read_by.description: Who resolves or connects to it.

precedence.description: Sources that set it, first wins.

unresolved.description: What happens when it does not resolve.

surface.description: One readable artifact the system leaves behind: what writes it, where, when, what it holds, how long it survives, and who can read it.

written_by.description: Contexts or code that write it.

contains.description: What a reader finds in it.

survives.description: How long it outlives its writer: none for a stream consumed as it is written, process_exit for a file that stays after the writer stops, forever for state that outlives the cluster.

mode.description: File mode, when it is a file.

failure.description: One way the system fails and where a human or another program sees it.

signal.description: What can be observed; [] when nothing can.

alerts.description: What raises an alert; [] when nothing does.

risk.description: Risk recorded for this failure, when one exists.

trust-boundary.description: Execution context (trust boundary); a node of one nested tree.

runs_in.description: Process boundary hosting it, when its parent is a logical boundary.

workspaces.description: kcp workspaces this boundary stands for.

contains.description: Overlays held here; system contexts join via their own context key.

principals.description: Who authenticates inside it, keyed by the credential they present.

enforced_by.description: Mechanisms that draw the line; [] when nothing does.

isolation.description: What the children share (os user, filesystem) and what process grouping is used for.

addr.description: Address and the variable or rule setting it.

client_auth.description: Credential ref a client must present, or none.

storage.description: Where the context keeps its state.

unsealed.description: Server comes up unsealed, with no unseal key held.

policy_from.description: Field whose value sets the sandbox's rules.

entered_when.description: Condition under which a process lands in this context instead of its parent's process context.

children.description: Execution contexts nested inside this one.

crossing.description: One call across an execution context boundary: the performer, running in from, reaches to.

from.description: Execution context the performer runs in.

carries.description: What is sent from -> to; [] when only returns matter.

gate.description: Checks the crossing passes; [] when none.

when.description: Conditions that must all hold for the crossing to happen; absent = always.

route.description: How the call reaches to: an address form, endpoint sources in precedence order, or a map of case to destination.

into.description: Where the carried data is written: field refs or object parts.

omits.description: Fields the performer has but does not send.

context.description: Execution context the weakness breaks; MUST be the crossing's from or to when crossing is set.

crossing.description: Crossing or crossings the weakness rides on.

anyOf.description: Several crossings with the same ends.

upstream.description: Upstream the weakness is about, instead of a crossing; every unpinned executing upstream MUST be named by one risk.

flow.description: Ordered application-level edges between system contexts.

reconcile.description: The provider's reconcilers: what each reads and writes, what wakes it, and what it runs.

wakes.description: How a reconciler is re-run, keyed by name.

applied.description: Objects that enter from outside the provider.

objects.description: Every system context with object applies <kind>.spec.

also.description: Specs created by something other than an applied example object.

model.description: Provider-wide reconcile facts, each code plus the structured facts that code establishes.

additionalProperties.description: One fact: code and keys naming what it establishes.

reconciler.description: One reconcile pass (on: reconcile) or finalizer teardown (on: finalize) of a kind.

reads.description: Whole spec or status read, to the subfields read and where the value comes from.

from.description: applied, or the reconciler that writes it and the wakes that re-run this one.

scope.description: Read wider than one named object.

unread.description: Own spec fields no reconciler reads; on: reconcile only.

select.description: How a list read is narrowed.

equals.description: Value the label must equal: a kind field ref or metadata.name.

admission.description: Admission gate in front of the pass.

lease.description: counting: admitted runs hold a lease that counts against capacity, not a binary lock.

runner.description: Context whose code performs the pass's I/O (kcp writes, process start, HTTP or OpenBao calls), or none.

target.description: Far end the runner acts on beyond kcp objects: the process it starts or the server it calls; absent when the pass only writes kcp objects.

rules.description: Conditional behaviour of the pass: rule name to the structured facts (conditions, precedence, thresholds) the code implements.

deletes.description: Objects this pass removes that are neither its own finalize teardown nor a status write: what is deleted, what triggers it, and how an object already gone and the workload process are treated.

what.description: Kind context or object whose object is deleted.

by.description: Who deletes it: this pass, the kind's owning pass, the pass of the run that supersedes it, or kcp garbage collection.

siblings.description: Which other objects of the same kind go with it.

trigger.description: Fields whose value sets the delay.

default.description: Value in effect when no field sets one.

base.description: Status field the delay is measured from.

then.description: Steps in the order this pass runs them, when more than the deletion itself.

process.description: What happens to the workload process.

already_gone.description: How an object already gone is treated.

teardown.description: Teardown detail of a finalize pass: the steps in the order they run, what is removed outside kcp, and the absences treated as already removed.

order.description: Steps of the teardown, in the order the pass runs them.

deletes.description: What the pass removes outside kcp objects.

if_gone.description: Things already gone that the pass treats as already removed and proceeds past.

wake.description: How a reconciler is re-run after another writes.

by.description: Mechanism: informer event, label fanout, direct enqueue, or requeue.

scope.description: Which objects of the woken kind are enqueued.

identity.description: The identity systems this repo touches, keyed by name, and the value forms where they meet.

meets.description: Value forms the identity systems share, and what carries each.

identity-system.description: One identity system: what holding it establishes, what it names, who can check it, where it is minted, and where it is implemented.

checked_by.description: Contexts that can check it; [] when nothing in this repo does.

minted_by.description: Contexts or upstreams that mint it.

minted_at.description: The moment it comes into being.

implemented_here.description: True when code in this repo produces it.

signature_verified.description: True when code in this repo verifies a signature over it.

methods.description: Methods the system offers, keyed by method name.

check.description: What a checker reads from it and which read decides.

decides.description: The read a verdict is decided from.

records_only.description: Fields read and recorded but not acted on.

identity-method.description: One identity method: what the identity is derived from and where its behaviour is implemented.

basis.description: What the identity is derived from; absent when it is minted.

implemented_here.description: True when code in this repo produces it.

identity-meet.description: A value form the identity systems share, and what carries it.

carries.description: Fields or objects carrying the value.

value.description: Literal value, when it is a fixed placeholder.

forwarded_to.description: Contexts or upstreams the value is handed to.

unread_by.description: Contexts holding the field that never read it.
